svg.title: Contract selection and who pays
svg.text: No procedure master list. The procedure
arrives as text on the Booking and is kept
As received from the surgeon's rooms
Short codes and snippets, exactly as sent.
Added beside the rooms' text when it
The wording the invoice prints, its own field:
from the Contract line's description, or the
Each Procedure on the Booking gets
the patient, or a parent or guardian
The insurer and approval number guide the
office's choice of Contract. The payer is
billed when the Contract's holder is not.
Every Procedure has exactly one Contract: it sets how the procedure is priced and who pays.
There are no kinds of Contract. A holder, a few settings and the lines make every arrangement.
A hospital, an insurer, a surgeon
For one anaesthetist or surgeon only?
None, one or many. Each sets a
fixed price, a rate, a discount
or RVG units, and may carry a
Bills the payer on the Booking
The one default Contract, offered first on every Booking: RVG units × the anaesthetist's own unit value.
A plain RVG Contract with no lines: most hospital and insurer Contracts look like this.
Dr B. Smith · Prepay price list
Bills the payer on the Booking
Offered only on Dr Smith's own Bookings, kept by the office from Dr Smith's list. Changing a prepaid price is open (OQ-96).
Bills the payer on the Booking
Each line stands alone. One Contract, linked to its surgeons by practitioner ID (OQ-105).
At booking setup the office's main job is
Only Contracts valid on the procedure date
whose holder fits this Booking, in this order:
Pick the Contract, then its line
Then the line, where the Contract has lines.
The insurer and approval number on the
Booking guide the choice. The Contract is
required: without one the Booking stays on
Mostly picked later by the anaesthetist, by
type-ahead; not needed on a fixed price.
Either way round: an RVG code finds the lines
that carry it, and a line fills in its default.
The Contract decides. Its holder is billed, or
the payer named on the Booking is.
Picking one starts the prepayment letter and
invoice, for the line's price, in full.
The anaesthetist can change the Contract
Until the List is authorised, from the same
filtered list, no explanation needed. Each
change is audited, flagged at office review,
and resets the price, rate and discount.
Pre-approval fell through on the day? Change
to No contract (RVG): the payer is billed.
